name: Shai Hulud
label: Revelation
lede: A band named for the sandworms of Dune found its first big singer in a fourteen-year-old, lost singers about as fast as it found them, and once tried to change its name rather than keep auditioning.

eras.title: Named for a sandworm
eras.text: Pompano Beach, Florida, 1995: guitarist Matt Fox and a few friends start a band and take its name from Frank Herbert's giant worms. Within a year Revelation signs them, the first singer quits, and a ninth-grader picks up the microphone.

years.h: Four friends in Pompano Beach take a name from Dune
years.p: Matt Fox on guitar, Dave Silber on bass, [[Damien Moyal|b655a47c-28f5-466d-aba1-4d607e4f598a]] singing and Jason Lederman on drums. Shai Hulud is the Fremen word for the sandworms of Arrakis.
years.xp:
The Dune joke runs through everything: the uncredited gang of backing vocalists who turn up on every Shai Hulud record are known as the Fremen Warriors.

Matt Fox has spent decades correcting two assumptions. According to Wikipedia, Shai Hulud has never been a Christian band or a straight edge band; members have included believers and atheists, drinkers and edge kids.

years.h: Halloween 1995, Discount's warehouse, fewer than 50 people
years.p: Shai Hulud play their first show at a South Florida spot Wikipedia calls Discount's warehouse.

years.h: Revelation's one worry: nobody could remember the name
years.p: A six-song demo reaches Revelation, and [[Unbroken|bebbd114-8e34-4035-a66e-37f9c144ca7a]]'s Rob Moran pushes to sign the band. The label asks for a different name. Shai Hulud keep theirs.
years.xp: Matt Fox told No Echo the demo went to a Revelation staffer named Jeanne, and that Rob Moran of Unbroken is the one who signed them. The records came out on Crisis, Revelation's imprint for heavier bands.

years.cap: As Friends Rust, with Damien Moyal singing, at Cheers in Miami, November 1996
years.h: Moyal quits for As Friends Rust, and a fourteen-year-old takes over
years.p: Damien Moyal leaves Shai Hulud and goes on to [[Morning Again|1b4e059e-856e-49a8-b7ca-c3ee67dcde23]], [[Bird of Ill Omen|23fca2fb-72da-4ccb-99b1-5f74652fec0b]] and [[As Friends Rust|2f106f2f-5990-4f50-9590-3fa8da941f98]]. His replacement, [[Chad Gilbert|4ed8c877-0036-44c7-bf6f-4c9c8e8ccedb]], is fourteen and nearly a decade younger than the rest of the band.

years.h: Gilbert's first session, with a Mario world-record holder on drums
years.p: Chad Gilbert records A Profound Hatred of Man with [[Steve Kleisath|faf2720a-5006-412f-8fb6-abef4bb696eb]] of [[Strongarm|039aebd3-83d8-4121-b7ed-5996bbf3518a]] behind the kit. Per Wikipedia, Kleisath also holds a Mario Bros. arcade record of over five million points.

eras.title: A kid screaming his lungs out
eras.text: Two records in a year on Crisis/Revelation put Shai Hulud on the hardcore map: heavy, melodic, oddly tender, and sung by a teenager. Then the teenager left to start a pop-punk band that sold far more records than any of them.

years.h: A Profound Hatred of Man sets the formula
years.p: Out on Crisis/Revelation with Gilbert singing: metallic riffs, melodic leads and a misanthropic streak Shai Hulud would keep chasing for decades.

q: We didn't know what the hell we were doing
years.h: Hearts Once Nourished with Hope and Compassion goes down in Tampa
years.p: Recorded at Morrisound in August and September 1997. Engineer Steve Heritage marveled that Chad Gilbert was screaming his lungs out, and two songs were built from leftover riffs days before the session.
years.xp:
Revelation handled the artwork and layout without the band. The first 5,000 CDs came out with the name misspelled on the spine as Shai Halud, and movie samples from Groundhog Day and Alien are woven between the songs.

Fox has never liked how it sounds; he told No Echo the band was "just a bunch of goofs" and he worried Gilbert would blow out his voice. It didn't matter: Loudwire put it on its 2020 list of the 25 best metalcore albums of all time, and bands from [[Poison the Well|5275425d-3cdb-4a9a-b9eb-3e246ec69881]] to [[As I Lay Dying|ba147ea0-60c4-4a40-9da6-0d5c2b2e7b03]] cite it.
play: Hearts Once Nourished with Hope and Compassion
My Heart Bleeds the Darkest Blood

years.h: Gilbert leaves to start [[New Found Glory|6acb932e-840d-47ac-8e0d-725ad8a6e52c]]
years.p: Chad Gilbert quits to form the Coral Springs pop-punk band that takes him to major-label stardom. He comes back to Shai Hulud more than once.

years.h: Fox and Gilbert write songs about the undead
years.p: Their side project Boddicker, later renamed Zombie Apocalypse, plays short, thrashy songs about zombies. The 1998 demo stays unreleased; the first album arrives in 2003.

years.h: Three songs, one split with Indecision, and a tour with Cannibal Corpse
years.p: The Fall of Every Man pairs three Shai Hulud songs recorded in May 1998 with the New York band Indecision. Around it, Shai Hulud tour with [[Strongarm|039aebd3-83d8-4121-b7ed-5996bbf3518a]], [[Bloodlet|754fcd17-fa48-428e-a2cc-f28d314a59e6]], Zao, [[Shadows Fall|2e3b75d8-00a8-486a-b4e7-a1f8f65e64c9]] and [[Cannibal Corpse|af8e4cc5-ef54-458d-a194-7b210acf638f]].

eras.title: A singer met on tour, a new home in Poughkeepsie
eras.text: By the end of 1999 everyone but Fox had changed. The band picked up a singer in Europe, moved from Florida to the Hudson Valley, and sat on its second album for about a year over the artwork.

years.h: Matt Fletcher moves from Oklahoma to Florida for the guitar spot
years.p: Guitarist Oliver Chapoy leaves and Fletcher relocates to replace him. He had first seen the band in Seattle in 1997, the night [[Andrew Gormley|32ee6b46-7d6c-4ea4-9b08-2cc64c8ac094]] was selling [[Kiss It Goodbye|f323fac7-b32e-49d5-b0ea-ef66fcf61416]] demos.

years.h: A Poison the Well drummer plays one show, then Gormley takes the kit
years.p: Steve Kleisath quits for personal reasons. [[Chris Hornbrook|43c22eda-8673-4347-a431-fa954ecc41ee]] of [[Poison the Well|5275425d-3cdb-4a9a-b9eb-3e246ec69881]] plays a single February show, then Gormley, ex-[[Rorschach|bfb77d72-8e36-4cf2-be10-7dcdd81d52b4]] and Kiss It Goodbye, joins.

years.h: The singer they met on a European tour stays
years.p: Fletcher handles vocals on the tour until [[Geert van der Velde|0b059231-2886-4338-9b60-c43d7bda2213]] joins full time. Back in Florida, founding bassist Dave Silber leaves.

years.h: A Metallica cover on a split with Boy Sets Fire
years.p: Crush 'Em All Vol. 1 comes out on Undecision Records with [[Boy Sets Fire|ba561cc7-2050-47d3-8bc2-c645a1393d90]], and Kleisath returns on drums for the one track. The same month brings A Whole New Level of Sickness, a split with Another Victim.

years.h: Florida is out; Poughkeepsie is in
years.p: The band relocates to the Hudson Valley, and the drummers keep rotating: Spikey Goldbach, ex-Inner Dam's Chris Cardinal, then Tony Tintari.

years.h: That Within Blood Ill-Tempered waits a year for its artwork
years.p: Produced by Jesse Cannon and finished in May 2002, then held back about a year over artwork disagreements. With no video and no radio, it reaches No. 39 on Billboard's Independent Albums chart.
years.xp:
It is van der Velde's only full-length with the band. He brought the first sung melody to a Shai Hulud album on the opener, Scornful of the Motives, and wrote Willing Oneself to Forget What Cannot Otherwise Be Forgiven.

Fox told No Echo the amps hadn't been serviced in a long while and needed new tubes before tracking, and he still isn't happy with the muddy result. He calls the record "a breakthrough in personal creativity", the one he's proudest of if not his favorite. A friend, drummer Jay of When Dreams Die, dubbed the sound Legacycore.

eras.title: The band that almost stopped being Shai Hulud
eras.text: The singer and drummer walked, and Fox and Fletcher decided not to quit. They decided to rename the band, and ran open auditions by mail for a new voice.

years.big: "Still finds Shai Hulud's message, style, and sound intact"
years.h: Shai Hulud announce they are now The Warmth of Red Blood
years.p: The band's own announcement, August 2004, after van der Velde and drummer Tony Tintari leave and guitarist Matt Canning exits for The Twilight Collective. Gilbert fills in for some shows.
years.xp:
Per Lambgoat, Fox and Fletcher began writing the next record under the new name. Applicants for the vocal spot had to be drug-free, at least 25 and dedicated to music.

The audition was by mail: download an instrumental of Whether to Cry or Destroy, record vocals over it, and send a CD to Fletcher in Poughkeepsie. [[The Dillinger Escape Plan|1bc41dff-5397-4c53-bb50-469d2c277197]] had used the same open-call trick.

years.h: Demos and live tracks, titled with a Kubrick joke
years.p: A Comprehensive Retrospective: or How We Learned to Stop Worrying and Release Bad and Useless Recordings collects demos and live tracks. Revelation and the band's own At Dawn We Wage War co-release it.

years.h: The rename lasts until a three-song demo
years.p: Eric Dellon sings and drums at once on a rough three-song demo. The band abandons The Warmth of Red Blood and goes back to Shai Hulud.

years.cap: Shai Hulud at the Camden Underworld, London, September 2006
years.h: Shai Hulud sign to Metal Blade
years.p: Friends in [[The Black Dahlia Murder|21f3573f-10cf-44b3-aeaa-26cccd8448b5]], [[Unearth|9f336c50-ae4c-4440-bda7-958aa12bc15a]] and [[The Red Chord|d1322057-e047-45ee-a573-769b37a395dc]] had already signed there.
years.xp: Fox told No Echo the move was strategic: "Having been somewhat stagnant in the hardcore scene for a while, it seemed like the logical next step." He calls Metal Blade a great label that stayed out of the way.

eras.title: Metal Blade, and the kid comes back
eras.text: The first Metal Blade record was built in ProTools, and Fox soon called it a misfire. The fix, five years later, was the singer from 1997: Chad Gilbert, by then a pop-punk veteran, came back to sing and produce.

years.h: Misanthropy Pure, played too perfectly
years.p: Matt Mazzali sings and Gormley drums. It reaches No. 15 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart.
years.xp:
Fox played every guitar part slowly and had it sped up digitally. He told No Echo: "The result is somewhat inhuman sounding; I certainly don't play that cleanly." He later called the record a bit of a misfire.

His favorites from it are the title track, Venomspreader and Cold Lord Quietus.

years.cap: Matt Fletcher at Vainstream Rockfest, Germany, June 2008
years.h: Van der Velde steps back in for Japan
years.p: Geert van der Velde sings a February 2009 run through Japan supporting [[Parkway Drive|a436dd02-0549-4c91-b608-df451217fdeb]] and Crystal Lake.

years.cap: Matt Fox at Vainstream Rockfest, Germany, June 2008
years.h: A split with New Found Glory and a title that runs 20 words
years.p: Not Without a Heart Once Nourished by Sticks and Stones Within Blood Ill-Tempered Misanthropy Pure Gold Can Stay is 500 copies, sold only on New Found Glory's Not Without a Fight tour.

years.h: Revelation turns 25 at the Glass House, and Shai Hulud play
years.p: Shai Hulud share the Pomona, California bill with [[Gorilla Biscuits|0320a32e-b781-40df-bf48-5cb5ee842762]], [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]], [[Sick of It All|e204ed91-3684-4561-b29b-d0b53f8459a7]] and [[Into Another|c235e5fd-4144-4e53-95ff-b33dc5f239c8]].

years.h: Fox says the fourteen-year-old from 1996 is coming back
years.p: Matt Fox announces that Chad Gilbert, now New Found Glory's guitarist, will produce and sing the new record.

q: It only took us 4 full-length albums to reach that hallowed place
years.h: Reach Beyond the Sun is Fox's favorite
years.p: Gilbert sings and produces, and Fox admits he worried again about the voice. Tours include Australia's Soundwave Festival that March.
years.xp:
Fox told No Echo the band was "firing on all cylinders" and that working with Gilbert as an adult was a different experience from 1997. He credits Gilbert with reining in his habit of writing overcomplicated songs, and says Metal Blade stayed out of pre-production and tracking.

His picks from it: the title track, To Suffer Fools, A Human Failing and At Least a Plausible Case for Pessimism.

years.h: Just Can't Hate Enough, with Moe Watson on drums
years.p: A new Shai Hulud EP.

eras.title: Singers come and go, then Geert comes home
eras.text: Fox and Fletcher kept the band going through a run of vocalists. Twenty years after That Within Blood Ill-Tempered, the line-up that made it shared a stage again.

years.h: Four singers in a few years, then 'Mean' Pete Kowalsky stays
years.p: After brief stints by Justin Kraus and Mary Carlock, Kowalsky fronts the band through 2020. [[Jay Pepito|5cfdf41c-fc3c-46cd-96f2-ec4da138c60a]] follows from 2020 to 2024.

years.h: The That Within Blood Ill-Tempered line-up plays Furnace Fest
years.p: Van der Velde and drummer Tony Tintari rejoin for the album's 20th anniversary at Furnace Fest, on a bill with [[Poison the Well|5275425d-3cdb-4a9a-b9eb-3e246ec69881]] and [[Underoath|674a7e8c-9682-419a-8e05-2358e28b5359]]. Van der Velde stays on as singer.
